San Jose Community Development Block Grant Program
The program reviewed by this document is the second of San Jose's three-year CDBG programs. The first block grant program contained components that were citywide in their applicability, in accordance with the objectives of the program, but concentrated the effort in three planning areas in which previous renewal, rehabilitation, and conservation programs had been initiated or in which the need for such programs had been identified. (Refer to Figure #2)
The new CDBG regulations strongly encourage the continued use of the neighborhood improvement strategy. The federal regulations refer to the designation of "comprehensive neighborhood revitalization" areas where activities are undertaken in a comprehensive program to upgrade the area. Specific activities vary by area, depending upon the condition and need of each. A comprehensive heighborhood revitalization program concentrates resource to upgrade an area affected by blight and physical deterioration, coordinates the efforts of public and private agencies and neighborhood organizations and is carried out in accordance with a local plan which provides for a coordinated program of physical development activities, necessary public facilities and services, private investments and citizen self-help activities.
The target areas covered by the neighborhood revitalization program are located in four of the fourteen planning areas into which the City of San Jose is divided: 1) the Central Area, which, as its name implies, is the area of the original City of San Jose where the oldest buildings and public facilities are located, 2) the Alum Rock Planning Area, which is located east of the Central Area. Urbanization in the Alum Rock Area has occurred more recently and more sporadically, and has been predominantly for persons of low and moderate income; 3) the Alviso community, located in the Alviso Planning Area eight miles northeast of the center of the Core Area of San Jose; and 4) the Willow Glen Planning Area, located south of the Central Area and containing a great diversity of sub-neighborhoods of varying condition and age.
A recommendation on projects to be funded by the block grant program is made by the CDBG Steering Committee. The San Jose City Council approves the final CDBG Plan. The eleven member Steering Committee is composed of one member each from the City Council, the Council of Churches, the Senior Citizens Commission, the City Planning Commission, the Citizen Community Improvement Commission, a member-at-large, two representatives each from the Alum Rock and Central Planning Areas and one member from Alviso.
On October 11, 1977, the City Council held a public hearing on the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) planning process and citizen participation plan. The adopted plan included both public hearings by the City Council and an extensive citizen participation process to determine community development needs and recommend projects for CDBG funding. The CDBG Steering Committee was directed to initiate the planning process and prepare a recommended three-year CDBG plan.
